_readme: Manually researched signals for the NorthStar Anesthesia ABM Signal Tracker, gathered via real web research (batch-by-batch, 5 companies at a time) while the permanent Sheets-based signal pipeline is being wired up. Each entry becomes one row in the 'alerts_sent' table via seed_northstar_signals.py. signal_type must be one of the canonical strings tracker/signal_score.py and tracker/dashboard_builder.py expect: 'Funding Round', 'Acquisition / M&A', 'IPO Signal', 'C-Suite Join', 'C-Suite Exit', 'News Mention', 'Product Launch', 'Partnership', 'Creative Hiring' (this last one is displayed to NorthStar as 'Anesthesiologists' via the hiring_opts override in build_northstar_dashboard.py -- the stored key stays 'Creative Hiring' so the shared scoring engine needs only one constant). confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, from the research pass) is written straight into the 'severity' column -- it is the closest available proxy for alert importance and is what actually drives the dashboard's H/M/L counts.

signals.signal_detail: Banner Gateway Medical Center (Gilbert, AZ) offering CRNAs a $50K sign-on bonus and $260K+ annual comp for an employed practice opportunity.
Banner University Medicine Tucson (w/ U. of Arizona) actively interviewing anesthesiologists at $530K+/yr, plus recruiting a CRNA Manager at $275K+.
Banner Health Community Hospital (Torrington, CO) recruiting CRNAs for an independent rural-hospital anesthesia practice at ~$375K.
Upgrading its entire surgical robot fleet to 49 Intuitive da Vinci 5 systems across AZ/CO/WY -- one of the largest such investments by any US health system.

Recruiting anesthesiologists dedicated exclusively to Jewett Orthopedic Institute via multiple concurrent postings across physician job boards, one of them seeking a full team on an M-F schedule with no call/nights/weekends plus a starting bonus. Sustained team-level need, not a single vacancy, at a high-volume orthopedic facility.
Open Director of Perioperative Services role for Holmes Regional Medical Center (515-bed, 16-OR facility) in Melbourne, FL, listed via Whitman Partners.

Own careers site has an open, actively-recruiting CRNA - Anesthesiology role at Springwoods Village ($191,500-$261,500), with further CRNA listings at the Main Campus, indicating a multi-site rather than single-vacancy anesthesia need.
Separately recruiting a Physician - Anesthesiologist (MD/CRNA Anesthesia Care Team lead model, no call/weekends/holidays) for its Houston ambulatory surgery practice.

Envision Physician Services / Kendall Anesthesia Associates (exclusive anesthesia group at Baptist Hospital of Miami since 1960) is actively recruiting General Anesthesiologists, a Cardiac Anesthesiologist, CRNAs, and a Certified Anesthesiologist Assistant, with sign-on bonuses up to $100,000.
Own careers portal lists open Anesthesia Tech positions in Miami and at the new Boca Raton Regional tower, signaling anesthesia-department staffing growth tied to facility expansion.
Carlos Hernandez named CEO of Baptist Health Doctors Hospital and head of Baptist Health Orthopedics, effective May 1, 2026.
Nathaniel Ortiz named CEO of Baptist Health West Kendall Baptist Hospital, effective May 1, 2026.
Center for Robotic Heart & Vascular Surgery added AI-powered 'digital twin' 3D heart-modeling software to plan cardiac surgeries in advance.
Broke ground on a new Medical Center in Pembroke Pines (60,865 sq-ft, ER and outpatient services), opening early 2027.
Caitlin Lewis promoted from COO to CEO of AdventHealth East Orlando.
Announced plans to build a new 80-bed hospital in The Villages, FL amid rapid regional population growth (opening ~2030).
Signed a letter of intent with Intermountain Health to form a Denver-area joint venture combining 5 AdventHealth and 3 Intermountain hospitals, expected to close early 2027.

NorthStar Anesthesia is already the CRNA/anesthesia staffing partner at multiple AdventHealth sites (e.g. AdventHealth Central Texas/Killeen, AdventHealth Bolingbrook IL) -- an existing account relationship, not a new prospect target.
AdventHealth Port Charlotte actively recruiting Board-Certified General Anesthesiologists and a Cardiac Anesthesiologist for its expanding anesthesia department following the 2025 acquisition.
AdventHealth Daytona Beach has an open CRNA position on its own careers site for its growing anesthesia team at the 367-bed hospital.
Invested nearly $350M in M&A and de novo development in 2025, adding 35 facilities to end the year with interests in 533 ASCs and 26 surgical hospitals across 37 states; targeting $250M for 2026 M&A.
Net operating revenue reached roughly $5.2B in FY2025 with EBITDA margins near 40%; Tenet's 2026 outlook projects USPI revenue of $5.5-5.7B.

Multiple live CRNA and anesthesia-support job postings across its careers site: Dover DE, Tucson AZ (Arizona Digestive Institute), Lake City and Summerfield FL, plus anesthesia techs in Dallas, San Antonio, Fort Worth, Waco, Arlington, Fresno, Tampa, and The Woodlands.

Atlas Healthcare Partners launched a new joint venture with Prisma Health to develop and operate more than 15 ambulatory surgery centers across South Carolina (Greenville-Spartanburg, Columbia, Charleston, coastal region) and southeastern Tennessee, transitioning two existing and two new Prisma Health ASCs into the JV. This is a newly named health-system partner distinct from the already-logged Banner Health JV, opening new anesthesia-coverage need across a growing multi-state ASC network.

Atlas Healthcare Partners and Fairview Health Services announced a new joint venture to develop and operate a network of ambulatory surgery centers across Minnesota and surrounding regions. CEOs Aric Burke (Atlas) and James Hereford (Fairview) both confirmed the JV; specific ASC count/timeline not yet disclosed. New named partner in a market Atlas has not previously served, representing a fresh anesthesia-coverage opportunity separate from the already-logged Banner Health JV.

Atlas Healthcare Partners, together with Banner Health, acquired the previously independent Surgery Center of Gilbert (near the Mesa-Gilbert border, AZ), rebranding it Banner Surgery Center - Gilbert. The facility has 5 operating rooms and serves Cosmetic, ENT, General Surgery, Orthopedics, Ophthalmology, Total Joint Replacement, and Urology, adding new named OR capacity with anesthesia-coverage need. This is a distinct, dated facility-level acquisition (a formerly independent ASC joining the network), not the previously logged Banner Health/Atlas JV-formation fact.

Houston Methodist's Department of Anesthesiology & Critical Care states its anesthesiologists and CRNAs 'collaborate with U.S. Anesthesia Partners' to deliver anesthesia care on the day of surgery, identifying U.S. Anesthesia Partners (USAP) as the incumbent contracted anesthesia group at Houston Methodist Hospital / the Texas Medical Center flagship campus that NorthStar would need to displace.

Houston Methodist Specialty Physician Group has multiple concurrent open anesthesia clinician reqs at its Texas Medical Center campus: three separate Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA) postings (JR-10613, JR-12066, JR-3994) plus an open Cardiothoracic Anesthesiologist role (JR-10232) for the cardiovascular anesthesiology team, indicating a sustained team-level self-staffing need rather than a single vacancy.

Kyle Stanzel, VP/COO of Houston Methodist West Hospital since 2018, was named CEO of Houston Methodist Clear Lake Hospital effective April 6, 2026, succeeding Carl Little, who moved up to CEO of Houston Methodist West - a facility-level leadership change at one of the system's 8 hospitals.

Ascension (nonprofit health system) completed its previously announced $3.9B acquisition of AMSURG, adding AMSURG's 250+ ASCs across 34 states to Ascension's outpatient network (Ascension now operates 300+ ASCs). AMSURG President/CEO Jeff Snodgrass remains in place. This is a full ownership change of the target company itself, which changes the buying committee/procurement structure for any anesthesia coverage decisions going forward.

As a condition of clearing the Ascension-AMSURG deal, the FTC required divestiture of 7 ASCs to resolve competitive overlap, including facilities in the Nashville, TN market (going to SCA Health, an Optum subsidiary, plus one Panama City, FL center going to Florida Gastroenterology Center). Nashville is NorthStar Anesthesia's own home market, so these specific facilities are changing ownership away from AMSURG and will need new anesthesia coverage arrangements under SCA Health/Optum.

AMSURG expanded its North Carolina footprint by acquiring five GI/endoscopy centers (Wake Forest Endoscopy Center, Wake Endoscopy-Cary, Wake Endoscopy-Raleigh, Clayton Endoscopy Center, Wilson Endoscopy Center), staffed by 15 board-certified gastroenterologists/hepatologists. Lower anesthesia acuity than surgical ASCs (GI sedation vs. general anesthesia), but represents new centers added to the platform needing sedation/anesthesia coverage decisions.

Live posting for Full Time and PRN CRNAs at the AMSURG GI Center in The Woodlands, TX. W2 compensation listed at $250,000/year, Monday-Friday schedule with no nights/call/weekends and a potential 4-day week - indicates a sustained, well-funded direct-hire need at this facility rather than a one-off req.
Live PRN CRNA opening posted for AMSURG's Melbourne GI Center in Melbourne, FL (no nights/call/weekends, part-time/PRN basis).

Texas Health Harris Methodist Fort Worth is expanding its Jane and John Justin Tower with 4 new dedicated obstetric operating rooms and a new Surgical Trauma Progressive Care Unit, alongside 71 new patient rooms (opening 2026), vertical build-out on floors 9-12 (completing 2029), and an 86-bed NICU (2030).

Texas Health Resources announced a new ground-up hospital on 51 acres in north McKinney, opening early 2029 with 60 beds (plans to double capacity for future growth), including surgical suites, a Women's Services Center with labor/delivery and NICU, cardiology services, and an ED.
CEO Barclay Berdan announced his retirement after 40 years with Texas Health Resources; he will step down as CEO in September 2026.

Winjie Miao named President effective April 5, 2026, positioned to succeed Barclay Berdan as CEO in September 2026, becoming the system's third CEO and first woman in the role. Laura Irvine was named SEVP and Chief Operating and Growth Officer in the same restructuring.

Envision Physician Services, Broward Health's anesthesia partner since the Feb 2025 incumbent transition, is still actively recruiting anesthesiologists, CRNAs, and Certified Anesthesiologist Assistants across all four hospitals roughly 18 months later, including an open Chief CRNA (leadership) role at Imperial Point ($150K start bonus plus relocation, overseeing scheduling, staffing, and recruitment for a 6-physician/10-APP team), with $100K-$150K sign-on bonuses system-wide. Sustained multi-site openings this long after the transition indicate anesthesia staffing has not fully stabilized under the current vendor.

Broward Health Medical Center added the da Vinci 5 robotic surgical system (the latest-generation platform, following an earlier rollout at Broward Health Coral Springs), continuing a system-wide robotic fleet upgrade that points to higher-acuity surgical case growth.

Novant Health completed its acquisition of Community Hospital of Stokes, a 53-bed critical access hospital plus a 40-bed skilled nursing unit and affiliated clinics, adding roughly 200 team members to the network. The county board selected Novant as its healthcare partner on March 23, 2026, and the deal closed June 1, 2026, expanding Novant's footprint into Stokes County, NC.

Novant Health filed a Certificate of Need application to add 225 inpatient beds via a new patient tower at New Hanover Regional Medical Center in Wilmington, NC, focused on heart and vascular care, including new advanced operating rooms, cardiac catheterization labs, and electrophysiology labs, as part of a $1 billion master facility plan.

Novant Health is directly recruiting CRNAs (self-staffing, not through its exclusive Charlotte-market anesthesia group) across multiple facilities and regions simultaneously, including a weekends-only CRNA III role in Winston-Salem plus open CRNA reqs in Wilmington, Huntersville, Matthews, and Kernersville, NC, indicating sustained multi-site anesthesia staffing need outside the Charlotte contract.

UMC Main (University Medical Center of El Paso) is directly self-staffing anesthesia: an active full-time CRNA opening lists $260,000/year employed or $301,600/year contracted, welcomes new graduates, and offers up to $10,000 in relocation assistance. Both employed and contracted tracks being offered simultaneously indicates sustained anesthesia coverage need, not a single isolated req.

_quality_bar.why: This feed drives real sales outreach for an anesthesia staffing and perioperative management company. A signal earns its place only if it changes who a rep calls, when they call, or what they open with. Volume is not the goal; a short feed of real buying windows beats a long one padded with press releases.
include_HIGH: The account is recruiting anesthesiologists or CRNAs itself (self-staffing, so displaceable or supplementable). Name the facility, comp, and whether it is one req or a team.
The incumbent anesthesia group or staffing vendor is identified (who NorthStar would displace).
New or added operating rooms, new surgical hospitals, new ASCs, OR or perioperative capacity expansion.
Surgical volume or acuity going up: robotic fleet purchases, OR throughput programs, a shift to higher-acuity service lines.
Ownership change at the account: M&A, merger, JV, PE or health-system takeover. Contracts get reviewed when owners change.
A new CEO, COO, CFO, CMO, or perioperative/surgical-services leader, or an open vacancy in one of those roles.
An existing NorthStar relationship or contract at the account (account-team context, and label it as such).
include_MEDIUM: Non-OR facility growth attached to a surgical hospital (beds, towers, attached ERs).
Financial growth or fresh capital that funds surgical expansion.
Division-level or MSO-level leadership change one step removed from the contract owner.
A single robot deployment or a single ASC joining a platform.
Instability worth a call: service-line closure, physician group attrition, ownership litigation.
exclude_always: Awards, rankings, 'best of' or 'most awarded' lists, Healthgrades/US News/Newsweek/Leapfrog honours, anniversaries, individual physician honours. Recognition is not intent.
Rollup or summary signals that restate specific signals already logged, and the same job req cross-posted to a second board.
Events superseded by a later logged event (log the current state, not the whole history).

Firmographics dressed as events: 'their site says they use X', 'person confirmed in role as of'. If there is no dated event, it is not a signal, and a today-stamped non-event never ages out of the 90-day windows.

Anything with no path to anesthesia demand: payer or health-plan network contracting, medspa and aesthetics, unrelated compliance settlements, venture investments in unrelated tech, academic faculty posts, PR and research milestones.
NorthStar's own job reqs logged as the prospect's hiring intent. That inverts the read: it means NorthStar already holds the contract, so log it as Partnership.
rules: Prefer specifics over aggregates. Facility name, OR count, comp figure, and date are what make a signal usable.
Every claim needs a real fetchable source URL. An empty category is a good and expected result; reporting nothing beats guessing.
signal_date must be the date the event happened, not the date it was researched. Use a today-stamp only for a genuinely live job posting.
Severity is importance to an anesthesia pitch, not confidence in the source. If most rows are HIGH, the tile has stopped filtering anything.

Exec-change signals carry a finite buying window of roughly 12 to 18 months. Past that, drop them to MEDIUM: knowing who holds the seat is context, not a trigger. Capacity facts (operating rooms, facilities, ownership) do not decay the same way and keep their severity.
Facility growth is HIGH only when it adds operating rooms or surgical capacity. Outpatient clinics, freestanding ERs, rehab towers, and medical office buildings are footprint, not anesthesia demand.
Calibrate severity to scale. A 49-robot fleet purchase and one da Vinci at one ASC are not the same signal; a 35-facility M&A year and one ASC joining a platform are not either.
A CEO transition is legitimately two rows (C-Suite Exit for the outgoing person, C-Suite Join for the incoming one): they are two different contacts. That is not a duplicate.
Prune as well as add. Re-run the seed with --prune so the JSON stays the single source of truth.
